blocking.title: N5 labels the interruption's own canonical cancel 'cancelled by the platform' and FAILs the drill: an item in flight at the SIGINT has NO first-run row, so torn_by_the_client({}) is False
blocking.evidence: certify.py:476 `torn = [item for item in cancelled if torn_by_the_client(firsts.get(item, {}))]`; torn_by_the_client (:461) needs a first-run row with a transport error_class. bench writes no row for an attempt the SIGINT cancelled: attempt() catches `Exception` (bench.py:887), not asyncio.CancelledError, so the cancelled task never reaches write_row. Reproduced: probes/sigint/repro.py - a slow SSE server, bench --rate 20 --requests 3, SIGINT at 3 s with all three mid-stream -> server saw 3 POSTs, bench exit 130, 0 rows. Box run2's own rows (results/E4B-box-4226315/run2-20260924T172244Z/work) show the shape: seq 7 (c3e9c044) first row failed/ReadError, seq 10 (643711ed) NO first-run row; both resumed stream_error_event/state_conflict/replayed. Re-judged at 88adae2 (rows re-classified as bench now records them): cancelled_replays -> (['c3e9c044'], ['643711ed']); resume_problems -> ["items cancelled by the platform (their first attempt was not the client's tear): ['643711ed5385eff08e8689ca7f1d62cf']"] -> e4b.a.dataset-resume FAIL. The same rows at 4db74b6 give resume_problems [] (probes/run2_old.log). So the round reintroduces a false FAIL of the cell R106 was made for, on the next box run (at 1.0/s with p50 ~17 s several items are in flight at the SIGINT). R106 (9b3b851) reserves the platform label for a platform-side cancel; an item whose key replayed (so it was sent in the first run) but has no first-run row was cut by the client's own exit. The lane's CANCELLED case models only the ReadError item, though its docstring cites the rerun's two torn items. Fails closed (never a false pass).
blocking.fix: Count a cancelled item with no first-run row as the client's tear (e.g. `torn = [item for item in cancelled if item not in firsts or torn_by_the_client(firsts[item])]` - verifier mutant vv_no_first_row_is_a_tear shows this passes every existing lane case), or make bench record the attempt the interruption cancelled (catch asyncio.CancelledError in attempt(), set an error_class such as 'CancelledError', write the row, re-raise). Add to the CANCELLED case a first run with NO row for the cancelled item (run2's 643711ed shape) expecting ([item], []) and a PASS, plus a mutant restoring `firsts.get(item, {})`.

nonblocking.title: admission_answer's Retry-After honouring and its 60 s cap are correct but unpinned
nonblocking.evidence: Behaviour (probes/test_polish_probes.py, urlopen and time.sleep monkeypatched): exactly 2 calls, then the second 429 is returned; waits '0'->0.0, '3600'->60.0, absent->1.0, '-5'->0.0, HTTP-date->1.0, 'inf'->60.0; 'nan' -> ValueError from time.sleep (unreachable: this gateway sends integers). Verifier mutants through the shared runner (verifier-mutants.log): vv_retry_after_ignored (sleep 1.0) SURVIVED, vv_retry_uncapped (no min(...,60)) SURVIVED ('2 passed'); vv_retry_any_refusal (retry any first refusal) died by exception (RemoteDisconnected when the fake server ran out of replies), not by assertion; vv_retry_every_429 KILLED at test_certify.py:396 (assertion).
nonblocking.fix: In the ADMISSION case, record certify.time.sleep and assert the waits (e.g. [0.0] for '0', [60.0] for '3600'); optionally a reply-count guard so an extra retry dies by assertion.

nonblocking.title: A second 429 in parity FAILs the cell under the label 'not refused as over the cap'
nonblocking.evidence: The second 429 returns {http_status 429, code capacity_exhausted, param None}; parity_check :438 `answer != OVER_CAP` -> wrong -> FAIL. That is right for parity (the cell must positively observe the typed refusal; parity runs on the idle box before the load cells, so a repeated 429 there is itself abnormal) and the answer is shown beside the clip, but the list label claims the clip was not refused as over the cap when it was never judged.
nonblocking.fix: Optional: list it apart (as the rungs do with over_cap_refused_for_capacity).

nonblocking.title: The report does not carry each client run's bound
nonblocking.evidence: Local report at 88adae2: no timeout field anywhere; load_cells/dataset_check keep only client(...)['exit'], so a future exit 124 does not name the bound it hit (run.shell's 'timed out after N s' is in the dropped tail).

nonblocking.title: measured.sop says 'none cancelled by the platform' in a FAIL that lists one
nonblocking.evidence: sop_property (:480) always ends 'none cancelled by the platform (R106)'; dataset_check writes it into measured even when problems exist. On run2's rows at the head: cancelled_by_the_platform ['643711ed'] while sop says 'none cancelled by the platform'.
nonblocking.fix: Optional: write sop only when there is no problem, or state the platform count.

answers.1_N12: certify.py:624-629 client_timeout_s = requests/rate + CLIENT_MARGIN_S (900) when --rate is present, else CLIENT_TIMEOUT_S 3600 (parity.py); client() (:632-634) passes it to run.shell; the soak goes through sampled_run -> client, so its bound is round(rate*14400)/rate + 900 = 15300 s at every possible soak rate (0.25/0.5/1.0 = half of a 0.5/1.0/2.0 supported rung). Box cells, computed with the runner's own functions and bench's seeded schedule (probes/sizing.log): envelope 135 req @0.5 -> 1170.0 s (seeded last arrival 276.3 s, +600 = 876.3, slack 293.7); @1.0 -> 1035.0 (138.2, slack 296.8); @2.0 -> 967.5 (69.1, slack 298.4); soak @0.25 3600 req -> 15300 (last 14218.1, slack 481.9); @0.5 7200 req -> 15300 (14458.9, slack 241.1); @1.0 14400 req -> 15300 (14348.4, slack 351.6); dataset resume 24 @1.0 -> 924.0 (first run keeps interrupted_run's 1800 s); overload 32 @1000 burst 32 -> 900.03; parity 3600. So no declared cell's schedule plus bench's 600 s request timeout exceeds its run.shell bound (smallest slack 241 s). Caveat: bench's --timeout 600 is httpx's per-operation timeout, not a total per request. Mutants: v_soak_cut_at_an_hour dies at test_certify.py:1259 AssertionError {'envelope-r0...sonl': 3600.0} == {... 15300.0}; schedule_ignores_the_rate :1259 (4500.0); no_margin_after_the_schedule :1259 (14400.0).
